messages:
Maria_CS: FYI — got an escalation from two enterprise customers (Telefónica ES, MercadoLatam) saying translations/regional responses got worse after last night's rollout. They pasted samples. This looks like a regression in non-English outputs, esp Spanish/Portuguese and Japanese. Raising to eng and ml.

Maria_CS: Customer quote (Telefónica): "Antes, cuando pedíamos resumen en español se devolvía un resumen natural y conciso. Tras el deploy de ayer, las respuestas son literales, con broken grammar and weird term choices (e.g., 'servicios telefónicos' -> 'servicios telefónicos (telefonía)' repeated)."

Maria_CS: Customer quote (Mercado): "Pedir una traducción de título marketplace devuelve inglés mezclado, sometimes full english sentences. This started ~03:10 UTC after release." :sos:

Akash_SUPPORT: Thanks Maria. Ticket IDs: #CS-1289, #CS-1291. Severity marked P1 by both customers because user-visible impact. They included reproducible prompts and outputs. I pasted their examples into the thread.

Akash_SUPPORT: Repro steps they gave (using Redwood hosted API):
```bash
curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-highperf-v4","input":"Por favor resume el siguiente texto en español: <long spanish article>","max_tokens":200}'
```
Actual output excerpt (customer):
"In this article, the main points are..." (entire paragraph returned in English)

Li_DEVEX: One quick sanity check: were any tokenizer changes rolled out or a new tokenization pipeline enabled? Also check whether locale detection fallback changed. I can run a small repro on my side.

Sam_ML: @Li_DEVEX @Priya_ENG tagging ML. Provide me the exact model name and the commit/deployment tag. I suspect either: 1) a model swap (wrong variant routed for certain regions/language headers) or 2) a postprocessing/locale mapping change that forces en fallback. Can you attach the request headers the customers included?

Maria_CS: Customers included headers. Example: "Accept-Language: es-ES" and custom header X-Region: eu-west. They also attached trace_id: trace-20240422-9a7b.

Jun_SRE: I'll pull routing logs for trace-20240422-9a7b. Also will verify which container served the requests. Offhand, there was a deploy to rwd-highperf-v4-canary at 02:45 UTC and then promotion to stable ~03:05 UTC by the deploy pipeline. @deploy-bot can you show the deploy events?

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline: rwd-highperf-v4 -> canary deployed at 2024-04-22T02:45:12Z by ci/cd. Canary promoted to stable at 2024-04-22T03:04:58Z (operator: autopromote). No manual rollback.

Priya_ENG: We intentionally changed the locale postprocessing rule in PR #4126 — it consolidated locale fallbacks into a single mapping to reduce variance. It passed unit/integration tests but maybe it over-generalized. The change was included in the canary. Rolling back is an option but want to be sure.

Sam_ML: Can we run a quick A/B: spin up rwd-highperf-v4@pre-PR4126 (previous weights + old postproc) and compare outputs on their exact prompts? I can run a diff on the eval set including Spanish/Portuguese/Japanese. Need the exact prompt payloads (Maria, can you paste raw payloads)?

Maria_CS: Pasted two raw examples from MercadoLatam and Telefónica in thread. Also note Mercado's user agent shows region us-south but Accept-Language: pt-BR. Both affected.

Akash_SUPPORT: Customers also reported sometimes the reply contains mixed-language sentences and odd token repetition. Some examples show the content being cut off then resumed in English. Could be a tokenization/continuation bug or fallback model with different tokenizer.

Jun_SRE: Routing log (excerpt):
```
2024-04-22T03:10:01Z TRACE trace-20240422-9a7b route-selected: rwd-highperf-v4@stable node=gpud-42 region=eu-west model_variant=fast-quant
2024-04-22T03:10:02Z TRACE trace-20240422-9a7b model-init: tokenizer=unicode-bpe-v2 postproc=locale-merge-v1
```
Jun_SRE: Note the model_variant=fast-quant and tokenizer unicode-bpe-v2. fast-quant was a new quantization profile we enabled for stable to reduce costs. That may change token boundaries in edge cases.

Sam_ML: Aha — fast-quant + unicode-bpe-v2 could explain language-specific token merges causing unexpected segmentation/merging leading to English tokens inserted when postproc fails. We need to test the pre-quantized model vs quantized. I'll run an internal repro against both quant profiles.

Li_DEVEX: For reproducibility, here's a quick script to run the same payloads (replace TOKEN):
```python
import requests
p = {'model':'rwd-highperf-v4','input':'Por favor resume en español: ...','max_tokens':200}
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json=p, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer TOKEN','Accept-Language':'es-ES'})
print(r.json())
```
Run twice: set header X-Quant-Profile: fast-quant or default to see diff.

Priya_ENG: I recommend immediate mitigation: 1) disable fast-quant profile for stable traffic (flip routing to default quant) and 2) create a targeted rollback of PR #4126 if tests confirm postproc over-generalization. Can we do step 1 now?

Jun_SRE: I can remove fast-quant from stable routing for the model in ~15 mins (will maintain canary). That should be low risk. Will monitor perf and error rates.

Sam_ML: Meanwhile I'll run batch diffs on a curated multilingual eval set (Spanish, PT-BR, JA) using the trace payloads + ~200 examples to compute BLEU/chrF and regression counts. If regressions exceed threshold we'll escalate to rollback.

Akash_SUPPORT: Communicated to customers: we are investigating, may do short rollback on quant profile. They asked for ETA — I gave them 2-3 hours and asked for more examples.

Maria_CS: Customer response: they appreciate quick updates. One customer provided additional sample in Japanese: "これはサンプルです。短く要約してください。" Actual output returned half japanese then english explanation: "こちらの文章では... In this article..."

Sam_ML: Preliminary local runs: default-quant output looks fine. fast-quant run shows token boundary artifacts on tokens with diacritics and CJK sequences, causing partial translation fallback to base english phrases in our postprocessing. Will attach diff log in 30m.

Priya_ENG: Sounds like fast-quant is the primary suspect. Jun — please proceed to disable fast-quant for stable traffic and keep canary until we validate. Also queue a rollback patch for PR #4126 as backup.

Jun_SRE: Actioned: removed fast-quant from stable routing at 2024-04-22T03:45:11Z. Stable route now using default-quant profile. Monitoring dashboards: tail error=customers/translation/regression spiked at 03:15 UTC, trending down after 03:48 UTC (partial).

deploy-bot: Routing change recorded by ops at 2024-04-22T03:45:11Z. No downtime.

Sam_ML: After switching quant profile, I re-ran the customers' payloads against stable. Results: Spanish and Portuguese outputs restored to prior quality in 92% of sample set. Japanese improved but we still see 4% mixed-language outputs (likely postproc edge cases). Attached diff csv (internal).

Akash_SUPPORT: Updated customers: told them we disabled fast-quant and are continuing investigation on remaining edge cases; asked them to confirm if quality returned to acceptable for their top 50 flows.

Maria_CS: Telefónica confirmed improvement on their most common flows, but flagged one long-doc summarization flow that still produced odd phrasing. They provided another trace_id.

Sam_ML: Next steps: 1) run targeted tokenization regression tests for CJK + diacritic languages; 2) revert PR #4126 if postproc still shows errors after tokenization patch; 3) add per-locale evaluation to canary gating. I will open a followup PR with proposed fixes and add tests.

Priya_ENG: I'll create a hotfix branch for postproc and add stronger locale unit tests. Also add a rollback playbook entry for future quant-profile promotions.

Jun_SRE: Monitoring will keep a watch window for 12 hours and will alert on any re-spike.

Akash_SUPPORT: Closing the customer-facing incident for now as "mitigation applied" — will reopen if they see further regressions.

Maria_CS: Thank you everyone. I'll collate customer confirmations and keep this thread updated.

Sam_ML: Uploaded diffs + logs to internal bucket path: s3://redwood-internal/multilang-regressions/2024-04-22/ (internal link) — includes script to reproduce both quant profiles and tokenizer dumps.

Priya_ENG: Filing follow-on story for product to include per-locale performance SLOs in rollout checks.

Jun_SRE: Marking incident P1 -> mitigated. Will convert to postmortem if residual customer impact remains after 24h.

billing-bot: Note: no billing impact reported for these requests.

Maria_CS: Thread summary for ops: root cause likely introduced by new quant profile (fast-quant) combined with a locale postprocessing change (PR #4126). Mitigation: removed fast-quant from stable routing; further fixes in progress.

Maria_CS: If you need any raw customer transcripts or direct contact, ping me.
